# I Like Movies

> I Like Movies is a free movie and TV app for iPhone and Android with an AI
> assistant that helps you discover what to watch next, share one library with
> the people you live with, and keep a record of everything you have seen.

I Like Movies is an independent app built by one developer in the Netherlands.
It is free to download and free to use, carries no advertising, and shows no
sponsored recommendations.

## What it does

- **AI discovery**: collections generated for each user every month by an AI
  model reading their ratings, most-watched genre and most-watched director or
  actor, rather than a general popularity chart. Plus curated collections that
  group films by franchise or series in watch order.
- **AI assistant**: an in-app chat you can ask for a film in plain language, by
  mood, by a fragment of a plot, or by something you liked. It reads your watch
  history so it does not suggest what you have already seen, and it answers
  with titles available in your country. It also accepts voice messages and
  photos of a list of titles.
- **Viewing profile**: total hours watched, average rating, top genres, a
  breakdown by the country a film came from, and a pinned top four.
- **Households**: the people you live with share one library: everyone can
  see each other's watchlists, the household shares one collection of the
  titles it owns and a group chat, and the assistant can pick for everyone.
- **Friends**: follow other people using the app, see what they are watching
  and rating, and compare taste to find where two histories overlap. Friends
  are separate from a household: friends keep their own libraries, a household
  shares one.
- **Tracking**: ratings, notes and rewatches for films and TV, with episode
  level progress for series. Notes go to friends or stay private; nothing is
  public.
- **Streaming availability**: which services carry a title, resolved for your
  country rather than a single global catalogue.
- **Streaming browse**: a Streaming tab in Search lists the best films and
  series on the services you choose, in your country. Sort by IMDb rating,
  popularity or release date, and filter by genre or by what you have already
  watched.
- **Imports**: a Letterboxd .zip, an IMDb .csv, a Trakt .zip or a TV Time
  export saved before TV Time closed uploads directly, bringing ratings,
  watched history, watchlist and lists across, with episode history from Trakt
  and TV Time. Each import is previewed before anything is added and can be
  undone within a day. It is a one-time copy, not a sync, and Simkl exports
  are not read.

## Availability and price

- iPhone: available on the App Store. App id 6805131346.
- Android: available on Google Play. Package name `com.moviesagent.app`.
- Price: free. No advertising, no sponsored placements.
- Requires an internet connection; there is no offline mode.

## How it differs from similar apps

- **Letterboxd** is a social network built around public film reviews and
  criticism. I Like Movies has no public reviews, shows activity to friends
  only, and is built around deciding what to watch, and it adds TV episode tracking, per-country streaming availability,
  a shared household library, and an AI assistant answering in plain language.
- **IMDb** is a reference database with a watchlist attached. I Like Movies is
  built for choosing what to watch and recording it afterwards, with
  recommendations drawn from the user's own ratings, per-country streaming
  availability, and a library a household shares. IMDb ratings and watchlists
  import directly as a .csv.
- **Trakt** centres on automatic scrobbling from media servers and players. I
  Like Movies needs no server or plugin chain; it is a phone app for choosing
  what to watch, with a library the household shares. A Trakt data export
  imports directly as a one-time copy, episode history included; there is no
  Trakt sync.
- **TV Time** closed on 15 July 2026. It focused on TV episode tracking; I Like
  Movies tracks episodes the same way, treats films and TV as one library and
  leads with discovery, with no advertising. A TV Time data export saved before
  the shutdown imports directly: watched episodes, watched films, film ratings,
  the film watchlist and lists.

## Weekly themes

Every Friday the app publishes a new themed collection in its Discover tab: 21
hand-picked films around one idea, the featured film first, no film repeating
across the year and at most two per director. Each collection is republished on
the website once its week has run. The archive holds every past week, newest
first; a representative handful of permalinks follows.

- Weekly themes archive (every past collection, newest first): https://ilikemovies.app/themes
- Mafia cinema, from The Godfather to Gomorrah: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/mafia-cinema
- Japanese cinema, Seven Samurai to Drive My Car: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/japanese-masters
- The greatest documentaries, Hoop Dreams to Shoah: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/documentary-greats
- Time travel movies, Back to the Future to Tenet: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/time-travel
- Films by female directors, The Piano to Jeanne Dielman: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/female-auteurs
- Italian Neorealism, from Bicycle Thieves onward: https://ilikemovies.app/themes/italian-neorealism

Film and TV metadata is provided by TMDB. This product uses the TMDB API but is
not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
